meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you think that's really possible?
It's realistic to do that in a day.

examples.text: Я не шучу и реально сваливаю отсюда.
examples.trans: I am not joking and am seriously getting out of here.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'belly, stomach' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Живот у тебя, как у депутата.
examples.trans: You've got a belly like a member of parliament.

заболеть.gloss: to fall ill, to get sick

meanings.en: to fall ill, to get sick
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'болеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall ill, to get sick', paired with 'болеть'.

examples.text: Вчера он заболел и остался дома.
examples.trans: Yesterday he fell ill and stayed at home.

examples.text: А у меня учительница по математике заболела.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'uh-huh, yeah', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'finger; toe' in everyday Russian.

Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'у-шеф'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sous-chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you a sous-chef or who?

examples.text: Тащи свою птицу су-шефу на стол!
examples.trans: Drag your bird to the sous-chef's table!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'along; by; about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'чество'). Common neuter noun meaning 'patronymic' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Agreed, simply Lev, without a patronymic.
State your first name and patronymic.

examples.text: Зови меня просто по имени, без отчества.
examples.trans: Call me simply by first name, without patronymic.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('understandable, clear').

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

examples.text: И выбираться он уже не может. Так, понятно?
examples.trans: And he cannot run for office anymore. So, is that clear?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

париться.gloss: to steam oneself in a bathhouse; (slang) to sweat over

meanings.en: to steam oneself in a bathhouse; (slang) to sweat over
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to steam oneself in a bathhouse; (slang) to sweat over', paired with 'попариться'.

related.gloss: to steam oneself at the bathhouse

examples.text: В субботу мы паримся в бане.
examples.trans: On Saturday we steam ourselves in the bathhouse.
What, are you steaming yourself? Harder, come on!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'course, progress; move, turn' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты предлагаешь вмешаться в честный ход выборов?
examples.trans: Are you proposing to interfere in the honest course of the election?

examples.text: Подожди. Ты предлагаешь вмешаться в честный ход выборов?
examples.trans: Wait. Are you proposing to interfere in the honest course of the election?

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to figure out
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order, official decree' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чальство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'management, superiors' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The management signed an important order.

examples.text: Успокойся, начальство просто не знает всей правды.
examples.trans: Calm down, the leadership simply does not know the whole truth.

examples.text: Официанты всегда обсуждают личную жизнь начальства.
examples.trans: Waiters always discuss the management's personal life.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'суждаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be discussed'.

related.gloss: not to to be discussed (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Yes, but orders are not discussed!
Yes, but orders are not discussed!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вышений'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('raise').

examples.text: Макс, надо у Германа просить повышение зарплаты!
examples.trans: Max, we need to ask German for a salary raise!

examples.text: Парни, да бросьте вы, какое сейчас повышение?
examples.trans: Guys, come on, what raise right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to celebrate, to note', paired with 'отмечать'.

examples.text: Я хотел отметить день рождения вместе.
examples.trans: I wanted to celebrate the birthday together.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'глашать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to invite', paired with 'пригласить'.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.
